data.headline: Short Treasury yields ease as small-cap futures positions remain divided
data.summary: The two-year Treasury yield fell from 4.80% on Wednesday to 4.76% on Thursday. For small companies refinancing debt, that lowers one benchmark. The rate an individual borrower pays also depends on the lender and the borrower’s credit.

bull.text: Leveraged funds trimmed their net short position in Russell E-mini futures from 55,080 contracts on November 3 to 44,429 on November 10.

bear.text: Over the same week, asset managers cut their net long Russell E-mini position from 23,623 contracts to 19,663.

watch.text: The two-year Treasury yield fell four basis points on Thursday. Bank loan rates and credit spreads would show how much of that decline reached small-company borrowers.

limitations: The futures positions were measured on November 10. A national Treasury benchmark provides no direct measure of an individual Russell 2000 company’s financing costs.
